output.summary: Across all 13 points, Phase 2 supplied strong conceptual boundaries and valuable distinctions between preparation, mutation, retention and publication. However, its 1,593 seed lines often function as implementation inventories, with repeated explanations and uneven abstraction. The final collection preserves much of this density across 78 diagrams and 2,645 lines. Expansion, placement and peripheral selection belong to later phases; Phase 2's contribution was the detailed, sometimes overgeneralized material those phases inherited.
strengths: The seeds establish useful identities and boundaries. diagrams lines 3–6 distinguish diagram, revision and local content identities; canvas lines 112–138 separate composition, exact revision bindings and personal view; storage lines 122–123 distinguish workspace and catalog publication. These distinctions remain visible in the corresponding final central diagrams.

Grouping adapts to several subjects successfully. source uses binding, mapped evidence, access, definitions and inspection; contexts separates conversation values, library operations, durable records, evidence and diagram bindings. Their final canvases retain these coherent functional divisions rather than organizing by filenames.

Important workflow distinctions survive compression: generation lines 66–82 separate prepared output from application acknowledgement; changes lines 32–35 separate workflow completion from acceptance; evals lines 67–74 distinguish retained output from accepting a proposal. These provide strong foundations for the final generation/batch, changes/review and evals/retain diagrams.

Ownership detail is especially useful where it explains behavior: editor lines 28–34 separate visible canvases from session and editor lifetimes; chat lines 82–87 distinguish active candidate controllers from retained histories. The final editor/session and chat/isolate diagrams develop these concepts effectively.

analysis explicitly distinguishes static call evidence from observed execution at seed lines 49–51, and separates dependency facts from partitions at lines 84–98. source lines 20–23 and 50–54, together with contexts lines 13–18, also preserve meaningful distinctions between content, range and descriptor hashes.

issues.evidence: runtime seed lines 38–100 enumerate a large constructor/service graph, followed by endpoint and error inventories at lines 113–151. Its final central diagram still devotes lines 27–71 to service wiring and remains 105 lines tall. storage seed includes debounce/retry timings at lines 44–55, writer concurrency at line 81 and cache capacities at line 152; its final central diagram retains many of these details at lines 30–35, 51 and 97. source seed similarly includes cache capacity and rendering chunk size at lines 75 and 92.
issues.impact: Phase 2 gives incidental constants and collaborator lists nearly the same prominence as architectural decisions. Later compression therefore leaves large central trees whose main story competes with operational reference material. Later additions contribute further density, but the lack of prioritization is already present in the seeds.
issues.recommendation: Regenerate around the decisions each point explains. Keep details that change the reader's model—such as separate publication boundaries, failure recovery or lifetime limits—and compress constructor inventories and routine constants into their governing behavior. Retain exact limits selectively when their consequence is important, rather than treating every available implementation detail as presentation-worthy.

issues.evidence: generation repeats retained-output retry behavior in seed lines 26–30, 66–82, 84–94 and 112–119; final central lines 45–60 and 73–76 still repeat it, with further treatment in batch and lifetime. agent-api repeats mutation recovery across seed lines 42–46, 79–83 and 116–119, retained in final central lines 37–39, 57–60 and 79–81. editor repeats controller state ownership and publication under seed lines 7–15, 21–34, 53–60 and 77–89.
issues.impact: Separate structural, call, ownership and dependency passes often retell the same mechanism instead of adding a distinct insight. This creates apparent breadth while increasing reading and reconciliation effort. The final peripherals amplify this inherited repetition, although their exact duplication is a later editing choice.
issues.recommendation: Give each mechanism one primary explanation within its seed. Add another perspective only when it contributes a new relationship, prerequisite or consequence. For example, explain generation acknowledgement recovery once, then make the ownership branch identify only what retains the prepared result and when that retention ends. Choose organization independently for each point.

issues.evidence: The same handoffs receive substantial treatment in multiple seeds: diagrams lines 76–89 and generation lines 39–53 describe candidate submission and revision issuance; canvas lines 108–131 and storage lines 26–38 describe checkpoint records and revision dependencies; editor lines 67–75 and agent-api lines 51–54 describe browser save/publication. These overlaps persist in final diagrams/source lines 19–26, generation/validation lines 18–23, canvas/restore lines 25–31, storage/central lines 17–38 and editor/boundary lines 2–17. source and contexts also discuss related evidence with different hashes: source seed lines 20–23 and 36–37 versus contexts lines 13–18 and 102–107.
issues.impact: Individual canvases are reasonably self-contained, but the collection lacks a clear division between the authoritative explanation of a mechanism and a caller's view of it. Readers repeatedly encounter similar flows while having to infer whether a version, hash, revision or acknowledgement refers to the same object.
issues.recommendation: Coordinate the seeds as a collection. Assign each shared mechanism a primary explanatory point and retain concise caller/callee contracts elsewhere. At handoffs, name the transferred object and identity scope explicitly—for example, document version, diagram revision, workspace revision, descriptor hash or source fingerprint. Preserve local context without repeating the full downstream implementation.

issues.evidence: runtime seed lines 83–90 nest LayoutTemplateService, ReferenceGenerationService, JudgementService and ExperimentService beneath EvalRunService inside an ownership-labelled service graph; final runtime/eval lines 2–11 distinguish constructor inputs from collaborators assigned afterward. generation seed lines 54–59 place sequential variant generation under 'Install according to operation'; final generation/central lines 33–42 separate preparation from installation. changes seed line 32 presents 'runAgentWorkflow: analyze -> materialize -> validate', whereas final changes/central lines 20–21 and changes/run lines 11–16 distinguish workflow execution from subsequent service validation.
issues.impact: Tree nesting and arrows sometimes blur injected dependency, ownership, execution sequence and conceptual grouping. The final outputs explicitly repair several such ambiguities. This is a Phase 2 relationship-modelling problem, independent of later layout; the supplied outputs do not establish source-level errors beyond these differences in representation.
issues.recommendation: Regenerate these branches with explicit relationship verbs and correctly scoped stages. Use containment only where it communicates a real grouping or ownership relationship; identify constructor inputs, assigned collaborators and callbacks separately when that distinction matters. Keep preparation, invocation, validation and publication boundaries clear without requiring a fixed set of relationship categories.

issues.evidence: Several seed statements are broader than their final counterparts. canvas seed line 55 says 'One gesture -> one saved checkpoint', while final canvas/central line 38 allows an unchanged view-only early return. chat seed lines 86–87 state settlement cleanup generally, while final chat/isolate lines 24–26 identify a preceding save whose failure can bypass that cleanup. contexts seed lines 60–61 say stale comment hashes fail, while final contexts/retry lines 15–19 distinguish receipt replay from a new comment's freshness check. analysis seed line 24 says the schema retains 'exported metadata'; final analysis/names lines 20–22 distinguish an optional field from its population.
issues.impact: Broad summaries can turn conditional behavior or schema capability into an apparent guarantee. Later phases spend presentation space restoring qualifications, and readers may still encounter a stronger central statement beside a narrower detail. These are observable differences between supplied outputs, not independently verified repository defects.
issues.recommendation: Preserve material qualifiers in Phase 2, especially around retries, cleanup, no-op behavior and supported-versus-produced data. State what is conditional on successful prior work, what is merely a contract, and what remains outside the evidence. Prefer a concise bounded claim over a universal statement that requires a later corrective peripheral.

issues.evidence: runtime seed lines 56–62 explicitly describe a shared CanvasApiProjection injected into live and agent services; final runtime/central lines 41–47 and runtime/context line 18 preserve that integration. agent-api seed lines 97–100 instead describes projection lifetime as the backend lifetime, while final agent-api/identity lines 21–24 says local defaults create separate instances and that supplied construction wiring does not prove sharing. Related evidence is also split between contexts final central line 77, which leaves fingerprint comparison to callers, and agent-api final central lines 91–93, which describes that caller-side status decision.
issues.impact: The collection contains complementary evidence, but point-local treatment leaves integration facts sounding unresolved in one canvas despite being presented elsewhere. The final projection disclaimer is a later-phase choice; Phase 2's missed opportunity was to encode the distinction between per-instance behavior and configured application wiring consistently across seeds.
issues.recommendation: Reconcile shared concepts across all seeds before regeneration completes. Describe projection maps as instance-owned in agent-api and identify runtime as the point establishing configured sharing. Likewise, connect context loading to caller-owned freshness checks through explicit boundary labels. Distinguish local evidence limits from collection-level integration evidence rather than flattening either into a universal claim.

issues.evidence: generation seed lines 19–22 gives runAgentWorkflow a top-level boundary despite stating that the supplied diagram runtime does not invoke it. The final generation canvas allocates a separate 16-line workflow diagram to that abstraction. Meanwhile, changes seed line 32 and final changes/run lines 11–16 show its relevant invocation. storage seed lines 149–153 similarly includes an 'Independent ImmutableRecords utility' while explicitly noting no calls from the pinned workspace/catalog implementations; final storage/blobs lines 14–20 expands it. contexts seed lines 76–89 already supplies a meaningful consumer of ImmutableRecords.
issues.impact: These inclusions suggest selection partly follows the available source bundle rather than the point's explanatory purpose. Explicit caveats prevent false integration claims, but disconnected utilities still compete with the active paths and encourage later peripheral expansion. The decision to allocate whole peripheral diagrams is downstream; their prominence originates in Phase 2.
issues.recommendation: Rank supporting abstractions by demonstrated relevance to the point. Give runAgentWorkflow its substantive explanation with changes and retain only a short scope note in generation. Explain immutable evidence storage where contexts consumes it, while keeping storage focused on its actual persistence paths and any useful contrast. Do not expand an unconnected helper merely because its implementation was supplied.

output.regenerationInstructions: Regenerate all 13 seeds together, preserving their successful functional boundaries and distinctions among immutable content, live state, captured evidence and publication. Establish a clear purpose and abstraction level for each point; prioritize consequential relationships over inventories. Consolidate repeated mechanisms within seeds, designate primary explanations across points, and label handoffs with object and identity scope. Correct ambiguous nesting and stage boundaries, retain material conditions on guarantees, and distinguish local component behavior from application wiring. Downrank disconnected helpers and routine constants. Use subject-specific structures rather than a uniform template or branch count. Treat the supplied final refinements as evidence of presentation ambiguities to resolve, not as independently verified source facts; leave layout, peripheral counts and routing to later phases.
